text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crash cripples Mir space station: Astronauts unhurt after docking attempt with Progress cargo vessel goes awry.
- Blair offers Sinn Fein new plan: Arms concession key to overture.
- Hunt for low-cost housing hard: Low vacancy rates push rents upward.
- Salmon deal is sunk for year: U.S. counterproposal faces rejection as both sides prepare to set own limits.
- Souvenir kitsch hot in Hong Kong: Shopping serves as antidote to anxiety.
- Family finds missing woman: Televised plea brings reunion in Florida.
- PanCanadian targets oil field: Pact with Saskatchewan paves way for C$1-billion plan to extend life of Weyburn deposit.
- Campeau's back! Berlin project launched: 72-year-old restarts real estate career after 7-year-exile.
- Central bank helps rescue sliding dollar: Action comes after currency falls third of a U.S. cent; analysts divided on whether higher rates justified.
- Bre-X debacle seen haunting junior miners for up to a year: But greed will eventually fix the game, conference told.
- Jackman plans to reinvest proceeds of National Trustco sale: Share buyback, dividend unlikely.

- BCI to go public in C$1-billion deal: BCE Inc. is set to sell shares in subsidiary Bell Canada International, raising cash for BCI's expansion in overseas cable television and wireless communications.
- Stocks skyrocket as investors bet on more financial takeovers.
